key_features: Facial chronically sun-damaged skin with asymmetric pigmented follicular openings, annular-granular and rhomboidal-like structures, and a blue-gray focal area, suggestive of lentigo maligna.
Large asymmetric dark lesion with irregular streaks/pseudopods at the periphery, blue-white veil and gray-blue areas centrally, multiple colors, and an eccentric light-brown structureless area.

Symmetric oval light-brown lesion with a regular ring of peripheral globules at the border (typical of a growing nevus), a homogeneous center, and only minor central grayish-pink areas, with no atypical network or irregular blotches.

Fairly symmetric round lesion with a regular pigment network that fades evenly at the periphery and a central hypopigmented area, consistent with a benign nevus, though the eccentric darker brown zone on one side adds mild concern.

A single-tone light-to-medium brown lesion with a patchy network, scattered peripheral dots and a central hypopigmented area, but no blue-white veil or multiple colors, favoring a dysplastic nevus over melanoma despite its irregular, lobulated outline.
The lesion is asymmetric and two-toned, with a pink-red half showing fine dotted and polymorphous vessels next to a brown half with an irregular network and blotches, on sun-damaged freckled skin.

Asymmetric lesion with irregular borders and multiple colors (light and dark brown, blue-gray, pink), atypical network, regression structures with blue-gray peppering, and pinkish areas with irregular vessels, all favoring melanoma.

Partially visible lesion with a fairly regular brownish network/globular pattern, smooth well-defined border, and uniform coloration without blue-white veil or atypical structures, favoring a benign nevus.

An asymmetric light-to-medium brown lesion with irregular notched borders, an eccentric pink-white structureless area suggestive of regression with fine vessels, and uneven pigment distribution on sun-damaged skin.
Small light-brown lesion with a central darker area, regular peripheral brown dots/globules, and symmetric structure on sun-damaged background, consistent with a benign (dysplastic/junctional) nevus.

Facial skin lesion with prominent follicular openings, asymmetric pigmentation, blue-gray areas, rhomboidal/annular-granular structures and irregular pigmented follicular openings suggest lentigo maligna/lentigo maligna melanoma; biopsy is needed to confirm.

A large, poorly defined lesion on sun-damaged skin with patchy, asymmetric light-tan structureless areas, irregular faint pigment islands and fine vessels raises concern for lentigo maligna-type melanoma, though the low contrast leaves real uncertainty.

Small lesion (about 4-5 mm) on sun-damaged skin with an asymmetric, eccentric dark brown blotch, irregular peppering/dots, reddish-pink areas and ill-defined borders, a pattern suspicious for early melanoma (likely in situ).

Small, symmetric, ill-defined pinkish-brown lesion with a central bluish-violet homogeneous area, fading edges and no atypical network, streaks or regression structures, most consistent with a benign blue or dermal nevus or a dermatofibroma-like lesion on a background of reticular solar lentigines.

An asymmetric, irregularly bordered brown lesion with uneven globules and network, plus central white scar-like regression and shiny white streaks, favors melanoma, though a dysplastic or congenital nevus remains possible.

Small, fairly symmetric oval light-to-medium brown lesion with uniform color, faint regular network and dots, and gradual fading border without regression, blue-white veil, or atypical structures, consistent with a benign nevus.

Pink, sun-damaged-looking background with irregular multifocal light-brown patches, central dark granular peppering suggesting regression, and prominent polymorphous red vessels, a pattern concerning for lentigo maligna or hypomelanotic melanoma rather than a benign keratosis.

Ulcerated, bleeding nodule with blue-white veil, milky-red areas, polymorphous vessels and an eccentric blue-black pigmented crust, suggestive of nodular or amelanotic melanoma, though a pyogenic granuloma or other bleeding nodule cannot be excluded.

Small lobulated reddish-brown lesion with a fairly regular reticular-to-globular pattern, uniform color without blue-white veil or atypical structures, and sharp but slightly irregular trilobed borders, most consistent with a benign nevus.

A large lesion on what appears to be sun-damaged facial skin shows a light-brown pseudonetwork with asymmetric pigmentation around hair follicles, scattered gray-brown dots, early rhomboidal structures and irregular, blurred borders, which together raise concern for lentigo maligna.

Ill-defined pink-tan lesion on sun-damaged skin with central light-brown structureless area and polymorphous dotted and irregular linear vessels, suggestive of hypomelanotic melanoma, though benign pink lesions remain possible.

Small, fairly symmetric oval lesion with regular reticular/globular brown network fading uniformly at the periphery and central darker hyperpigmentation, without blue-white veil, regression, or atypical streaks.

Light-brown lesion with a fairly regular, uniform reticular-globular pigment network, only two colors, and no blue-white veil, regression or atypical vessels, though its bilobed irregular outline adds some concern.
Fairly uniform light-to-medium brown lesion with a regular fine reticular network, mild shape asymmetry but no blue-white veil, atypical dots, streaks, or regression, consistent with a benign nevus.

An asymmetric, dark brown lesion with irregular, unevenly distributed peripheral streaks and pseudopods, blotchy central pigmentation and an irregular border favor melanoma over a symmetric Reed (Spitz) nevus.

Asymmetric, irregularly shaped brown lesion with an atypical pigment network, eccentric dark dots/globules in the upper right, and regression-like hypopigmented areas; these favor melanoma, though a dysplastic nevus remains possible.

Small, fairly symmetric dark brown-purple lesion with a darker central blotch fading to a lighter brown periphery, with no clear atypical network, regression structures, or multiple colors; hair obscures detail, so moderate uncertainty remains.

A large, asymmetric light-brown lesion with a central white scar-like area suggesting regression, irregular eccentric brown blotches, and an uneven patchy reticular network, though dermatofibroma or a regressing nevus remain possible.

Large asymmetric lesion with irregular, notched borders, multiple colors (dark brown, light brown, blue-gray), a blue-white veil and regression-like areas, and an irregular, disorganized pigment pattern.

Small (~3-4 mm), oval, fairly symmetric brown lesion with a regular pigment pattern, a slightly darker eccentric dot cluster, and a smooth light-brown periphery, without atypical network, regression structures or blue-white veil, favoring a benign nevus.

Large, asymmetric lesion on chronically sun-damaged facial skin with multiple colors (tan, dark brown, black, blue-gray), atypical pigment network, a dark blue-black blotch with blue-white structures, and irregular annular-granular pattern around follicles, suggestive of lentigo maligna melanoma.

Asymmetric brown lesion with an irregular eccentric extension and an off-center blue-gray to pinkish area showing blue-white veil-like structureless zones and scattered gray dots (peppering), which favors melanoma over a benign nevus.
Central blue-white veil with regression-like white scar areas, asymmetric multicomponent pigmentation, irregular brown-gray peripheral blotches, and polymorphous pinkish vascular background.
Asymmetric lesion with irregular borders, multiple brown-orange-red colors, peripheral red dots/globules, a central whitish blue-gray veil-like structureless area, and irregular pigment distribution.

A pink, largely amelanotic lesion with polymorphous dotted and irregular linear vessels, milky-red structureless areas and white structureless zones, without a clear benign pattern, raises concern for amelanotic melanoma.

Large featureless pink-milky red area with shiny white lines, faint dotted and polymorphous vessels, and irregular residual brown blotches on sun-damaged skin, raising concern for hypomelanotic or regressing melanoma over a benign lichenoid keratosis.

A fairly symmetric lesion ringed by regular peripheral brown globules and pseudopods in a starburst, Spitz/Reed-like growth pattern, though the central blue-gray to purple area with dark dots keeps melanoma risk moderate.

Fairly symmetric tan-brown lesion with a regular, fine reticular network that thins out peripherally, central hypopigmentation with a few scattered dots, and no blue-white veil, regression structures, or atypical vessels, favoring a dysplastic or compound nevus; the blue-gray marks at the top edge are skin-marker ink outside the lesion.

The lesion has an asymmetric, irregularly notched outline with a thickened pigment network, but the network is fairly organized with mostly regular meshes and fades evenly at the edges, with only small pale central areas and no blue-white veil, atypical dots, or streaks, which favors an atypical (dysplastic) nevus over melanoma.

Oval, fairly symmetric light-brown lesion with peripheral small globules/dots around a pinkish-violet central area with milia-like cysts and fine vessels; the regular pattern favors a benign (likely dysplastic/compound) nevus, though the pinkish center and peripheral dots warrant some caution.

Exophytic, papillomatous cobblestone-like lobulated surface with skin-colored globular clods, focal light brown pigment, symmetric outline and no atypical network or blue-white veil, favoring a congenital/dermal papillomatous nevus.

Small, fairly symmetric brown macule with a darker central zone, a smooth fading periphery and no regression, blue-white veil or atypical network, consistent with a benign nevus alongside a similar neighboring lesion.

A small brown lesion on sun-damaged skin with an asymmetric shape, irregular notched borders, and an eccentric darker blotch against lighter brown pigment raises concern for early melanoma or melanoma in situ, though a dysplastic nevus or solar lentigo remains possible.
Large asymmetric lesion with eccentric dark brown-black area showing blue-gray veil-like structureless zones, irregular pigment distribution, multiple colors, and an irregular, partly blurred border.

Broad longitudinal melanonychia band with heterogeneous brown-to-gray-black pigmentation, irregular lines of varying color and width, and fine dark granules, suggesting subungual melanoma; a benign nail band remains possible, so biopsy is warranted.

A faint, ill-defined light-brown lesion on sun-damaged skin, with an eccentric darker brown irregular blotch, angulated asymmetric pigmentation and a pinkish regression-like area, suggestive of lentigo maligna.
Asymmetric lesion with an eccentric dark blue-black blotch, blue-gray veil-like area, irregular atypical network/globules and ill-defined borders on a reddish background.
The lesion is asymmetric with irregular, angulated borders, uneven brown pigmentation, eccentric darker areas, and blue-gray peppering suggesting regression.

A large, fragmented, asymmetric light-to-dark brown lesion on sun-damaged pink skin shows irregular islands of pigment, gray-brown peppering/granularity, and whitish regression-like areas, which together suggest lentigo maligna or a regressing melanoma over a benign keratosis.

Irregular, asymmetric light-brown lesion with an atypical, broken network, irregular peripheral dots/globules, a central whitish regression-like area, and pinkish vascular areas on sun-damaged skin, raising concern for early melanoma.

Small light-brown lesion with a fairly uniform, delicate reticular pattern, mildly irregular notched outline, no blue-white veil, atypical network, or regression structures, most consistent with a benign nevus.

A faint, pale pink-tan macule with a soft light-brown blotch, regular dotted vessels, and no atypical network, regression, or blue-white structures, which favors a benign lesion such as a lightly pigmented nevus or lentigo; the surrounding pen markings and air bubbles are artifacts.
Asymmetric, irregularly shaped lesion with multiple colors (light brown, dark brown, eccentric blue-gray blotch), irregular structureless areas and a fragmented, poorly defined border.

The lesion is small and brown with a bilobed outline, and its fairly regular radial streaks around the periphery suggest a starburst (Reed/Spitz-type) pattern, though the asymmetry and peripheral streaks keep melanoma a real possibility.

Large, fairly symmetric brown lesion with a mostly regular pigment network, multifocal darker patches and central lighter areas, without blue-white veil, regression structures or irregular streaks, favoring a dysplastic or benign nevus.

Small light-to-medium brown lesion with a fairly uniform faint reticular/globular pattern and gradual fading edges, only mild irregularity of central darker blotches and no blue-white veil or atypical vessels, favoring a benign nevus.

A large, asymmetric, ill-defined light-to-dark brown lesion with irregular blotchy pigmentation, a focal darker irregular network with dots, whitish regression-like areas and pinkish erythema with fine vessels, extending beyond the field on sun-damaged skin, is suspicious for melanoma in situ.

Small light-to-medium brown lesion with a fairly uniform faint reticular/homogeneous pattern, mild irregular outline but no blue-white veil, regression, atypical vessels or multiple colors, set in background of solar lentigines, favoring a benign nevus or lentigo.
Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (tan, brown, red, blue-gray), irregular blotches, blue-white/gray peppering and regression-like whitish central areas, and irregular borders.
An asymmetric, multicomponent lesion with irregular brown blotches and a streak-like periphery around a central pink, regression-like area containing dotted and irregular vessels.
Asymmetric lesion with an atypical, irregularly fading pigment network, an eccentric darker brown-gray center with blue-gray areas, whitish regression-like zones, and an irregular dark dot.
Small (~5 mm) light-brown lesion with fairly symmetric radial/reticular pigmentation, a central pinkish area, and a soft fading border, most consistent with a benign nevus despite mild irregularity.
Small but asymmetric lesion with a blue-white veil-like area, irregular dark brown globules and an atypical network, set within an uneven, faint brown peripheral pigmentation.

Ill-defined, asymmetric brown pigmentation on sun-damaged facial skin with follicular openings, asymmetric perifollicular pigmentation, gray-blue dots and regression-like white areas, suggestive of lentigo maligna.

Asymmetric lesion with irregular notched borders, multiple colors (dark brown, black, red-pink), irregular peripheral dots/globules and pseudopod-like projections, a central blue-black blotch, and pinkish regression-like areas.

A pink-red amelanotic papule/nodule with no pigment network and polymorphous dotted and irregular linear vessels raises concern for amelanotic melanoma, although Spitz or dermal nevus remains possible.

Small asymmetric brown lesion on sun-damaged skin with an eccentric blue-gray area showing peppering/granularity, regression-like structures and irregular pigment distribution, favoring early melanoma.
The lesion is asymmetric with an irregular, notched border, uneven brown pigmentation with irregular dark dots and globules, and central blue-gray and whitish regression-like areas.

Pink erythematous macule with a small central erosion/crust, dotted vessels and only faint scattered tan pigment without atypical network, streaks or blue-white structures, suggesting an inflamed or traumatized benign lesion, though amelanotic melanoma cannot be fully excluded.

The lesion is asymmetric and irregularly bordered, pink-red and largely hypomelanotic, with diffuse dotted vessels, a central reddish focus and an irregular light-brown periphery, which together raise concern for amelanotic or hypomelanotic melanoma over a benign lesion.

A uniformly light-brown, map-like patch with sharply scalloped, moth-eaten borders on sun-damaged skin with telangiectasias favors solar lentigo, but the irregular polycyclic outline keeps lentigo maligna a real possibility.

An eccentric black blotch with peripheral pseudopods and streaks sits within a larger asymmetric light-brown lesion that has irregular dots and globules, a focal pinkish-red area and multiple colors, a pattern suspicious for melanoma arising in a nevus.
Asymmetric, irregularly outlined brown lesion on sun-damaged skin with uneven pigment, a central pinkish-gray regression-like zone with granularity and white structures, and an atypical network.

Asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (light brown, dark brown, blue-gray), an eccentric blue-white/gray veil-like area, irregular dots/globules and an irregular, blurred border on sun-damaged facial skin.
Asymmetric lesion with irregular, broadened atypical pigment network, multiple eccentric dark blotches, blue-gray areas and irregular notched borders suggest melanoma.
Small (~5 mm), roughly symmetric oval lesion with uniform orange-brown color, regular fine pigment network/globular pattern and smooth fading borders, consistent with a benign nevus.

Large, close-up view of a heavily pigmented lesion with a structureless blue-black area, irregular blotchy pigmentation and an asymmetric, poorly defined border fading into reddish-brown skin with atypical dots and globules, which favors melanoma.

Small light-to-medium brown lesion with a fairly regular reticular/globular pattern and a slightly darker center, mildly irregular fragmented border, no blue-white veil, atypical vessels or regression; most consistent with a benign nevus.
Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors, central blue-white veil and gray regression, irregular peripheral streaks/pseudopods, and scattered irregular dots and globules at the periphery.

The lesion shows marked asymmetry, an atypical pigment network with irregular dark dots and an eccentric dark blotch, a central whitish regression-like area, and detached peripheral pigmented islands with uneven brown shades.

Large, ill-defined lesion with an atypical, broken pigment network, irregular dark blotches with blue-gray areas and dots, extensive white regression-like areas, and multiple colors on sun-damaged skin, suggesting melanoma (likely lentigo maligna type).

Small, faint light-brown lesion with regularly distributed brown dots/globules and a slightly darker central area on pink skin, no atypical network, blue-white veil or regression, consistent with a benign nevus.

Small, fairly symmetric brown lesion with a regular pigment network fading evenly at the periphery and only a few central dark dots, consistent with a benign nevus despite a few slightly irregular edge projections.

Ill-defined light brown lesion on sun-damaged skin with an irregular, asymmetric pigment network, a darker eccentric area with fine gray dots, and a polymorphous red vascular pattern, suggesting lentigo maligna or melanoma in situ.

Asymmetric lesion with irregular, notched borders, eccentric dark-brown to black irregular dots and streak-like radial projections, and central blue-white/whitish structureless areas suggesting regression.

Small, fairly symmetric light-to-medium brown lesion with a regular reticular network, central darker hyperpigmentation fading evenly to the periphery, and no blue-white veil, atypical vessels or irregular streaks, consistent with a benign nevus.

The pigmentation is asymmetric with blurred borders, and irregular dark-brown and gray-violet dots and globules cluster at the right periphery, alongside a bluish-gray structureless veil-like area, suggesting atypia.

The lesion is asymmetric, with an eccentric dark brown-black central blotch, an irregular, patchy pigment network that fades unevenly at the periphery, and poorly defined, irregular borders with several shades of brown.

Tiny (~2-3 mm) light-brown lesion with a darker central hub, symmetric faint peripheral pigmentation, and no atypical network, regression, or blue-white structures, set among similar background lentigines; this is most consistent with a benign nevus or lentigo.

Asymmetric brown lesion on sun-damaged facial skin with an eccentric dark blotch, irregular borders and a faint granular light-brown extension around follicular openings, raising concern for lentigo maligna, though pigmented actinic keratosis or solar lentigo remain plausible.

Small brown lesion with mildly irregular blotchy pigmentation and scattered dots but fairly symmetric overall shape, a single color tone, and no regression, blue-white veil, or atypical network, favoring a benign (possibly dysplastic) nevus over melanoma.

A poorly defined pink-to-orange patch on sun-damaged skin with no pigment network, fine linear and reticular background vessels and a few faint red dots; amelanotic melanoma cannot be excluded, but I lean toward a benign keratinocytic or inflammatory lesion.
Sun-damaged facial skin with irregular brown pigment and gray granules surrounding follicular openings in an asymmetric, annular-granular pattern, which raises concern for lentigo maligna.
Asymmetric, irregularly bordered lesion with several colors (brown, purple, blue-gray), a central blue-white veil-like area, and irregular peripheral dots and globules.

Small, faint pinkish-tan macule with homogeneous light brown-red pigmentation, fairly regular borders, no atypical network, blue-white veil, or regression structures, suggesting a benign nevus, though the hypopigmented, pink appearance keeps some suspicion.

A largely pink, hypopigmented lesion shows polymorphous dotted and linear-irregular vessels on a milky-pink background, with asymmetric, irregular brown blotches and dots, which raises concern for (hypo)amelanotic melanoma, though superficial basal cell carcinoma is a differential.
Asymmetric lesion with irregular lobulated borders, multiple brown shades, peripheral dots and globules, irregular streak-like projections, and a central bluish-gray structureless area.

Scalp lesion with central white scar-like regression area surrounded by peppering/blue-gray granules, faint pinkish vessels, and an additional gray-blue area at the periphery, suggestive of a regressing melanoma.

A large, ill-defined, asymmetric patch on what looks like sun-damaged facial skin, with prominent follicular openings, an irregular eccentric dark-brown blotch with greyish dots, multiple shades of brown and pink, and whitish regression-like areas, suggestive of lentigo maligna.

An irregular, asymmetric lesion on sun-damaged skin with surrounding lentigines, showing light-to-dark brown structureless pigment, an eccentric pink-red area with dotted vessels, and uneven borders, which together raise concern for lentigo maligna or early melanoma over a benign lentigo or LPLK.

Elongated, mildly asymmetric brown lesion with a fairly regular faded pigment network, a few darker central clods, and a smooth gradual border, consistent with a dysplastic/compound nevus; it lacks blue-white veil, regression, or atypical vessels, though the asymmetry and focal darker areas keep melanoma possible.

Small, fairly symmetric light-brown lesion with a regular pigment network that fades evenly at the periphery, a few central dots and no blue-white veil or atypical structures, consistent with a benign nevus.

Asymmetric lesion with irregular eccentric dark-brown pigmentation and blotches in the upper half, plus an unpigmented pink-red lower zone with dotted/polymorphous vessels and whitish areas, suggesting multicomponent pattern concerning for melanoma.

Brown lesion with a mostly regular reticular network, mild asymmetry and irregular borders, and a few darker blotchy, faintly grayish areas, without clear regression or atypical vessels, favoring a (possibly dysplastic) nevus over melanoma.
Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (light and dark brown, blue-gray, pink), blue-white veil, regression structures with peppering, irregular dots and globules, and a pink scar-like area.

Light-to-medium brown lesion with uniform color and a fairly symmetric reticular/globular pattern that fades gradually at a slightly irregular, fuzzy border, with no blue-white veil, regression, or atypical vessels, favoring a benign nevus.

Asymmetric lesion on sun-damaged skin with irregular borders, multiple colors (light brown, dark brown, black-blue), eccentric irregular dark dots/globules, and focal regression-like gray-white areas.

A small (~3 mm), excoriated lesion with a central serous-hemorrhagic crust, faint light-brown peripheral pigmentation and surrounding erythema, without atypical network, regression structures or blue-white veil, most consistent with a traumatized benign nevus or lentigo.

An asymmetric, multicomponent light-brown macule on sun-damaged skin, with an irregular, broken pigment network, a central whitish regression-like area, irregular streak-like projections and separate pigmented islands, suggests melanoma in situ.

Small, fairly symmetric, sharply demarcated dark brown lesion with a regular peripheral pigment network fading at the edges and no blue-white veil, atypical vessels, or irregular streaks, consistent with a benign (likely Reed/junctional) nevus.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (brown, dark brown, blue-gray), a blue-white veil, white scar-like regression area, irregular blotches and dots, and scale/crust, all favoring invasive melanoma over a seborrheic keratosis.

Small lesion with a fairly regular reticular pigment network that fades evenly at the periphery and has two shades of brown, though the irregular bilobed shape and darker central area add mild concern; most consistent with a dysplastic/compound nevus.

Dark, somewhat asymmetric lesion with irregular radial streaks, unevenly distributed peripheral dots and globules, and focal blue-gray areas around a darker eccentric center; a pigmented Spitz/Reed nevus is the main benign alternative.

Asymmetric, irregularly bordered lesion on sun-damaged skin with multiple colors (brown, gray-blue, pink), peppering/granularity, an off-center blue-gray area, and a pink regression-like extension, all suggesting melanoma (possibly in situ/lentigo maligna type).

Small, fairly symmetric oval brown lesion with a darker central zone, smooth fading periphery and no atypical network, regression, or blue-white structures, consistent with a benign nevus (purple marker ink and hair are artifacts).

Small light-brown lesion with a fairly regular, fine pigment network that fades gradually at the periphery, a single uniform tan-brown color, and no blue-white veil, atypical dots or regression structures, most consistent with a benign nevus.
Large lesion with extensive regression (white-pink scar-like areas with peppering), irregular asymmetric brown pigmentation, irregular dots/globules, and polymorphous fine vessels suggest melanoma.

Fairly symmetric brown lesion with a regular pigment network fading at the periphery and only mild central darker blotches, without clear regression structures, blue-white veil, or atypical vessels, favoring a benign (possibly dysplastic) nevus.

Irregular, asymmetric brown-black pigmentation with angulated/zigzag pattern and faint peripheral tan pigment on chronically sun-damaged facial (ear/periauricular) skin with telangiectasia, suggestive of lentigo maligna.
Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (brown, red, blue-gray/purple), irregular dark blotches, regression-like whitish areas, and an atypical, irregularly fading network.

An asymmetric brown macule on sun-damaged skin with an irregular, notched border, a pinkish central area suggesting regression, uneven pigment and a few eccentric dark dots raises concern for early or in situ melanoma, though a dysplastic nevus remains possible.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (dark brown, black, red, blue-gray), irregular black dots and globules at the periphery, a blue-white veil, white scaly areas, and an ulcerated, hemorrhagic-appearing dark red zone.
Asymmetric lesion with irregular borders, multiple colors (light brown, dark brown, reddish, blue-gray), irregular peripheral dots/globules, and a central blue-white veil-like area with regression.

This is a raised, symmetric-outlined nodule showing several colors: a blue-white veil, an eccentric black-brown blotch, scattered red dots and globules, and irregular dark dots, which together suggest nodular melanoma over a blue nevus.

Asymmetric, irregularly bordered lesion with multiple brown shades, an eccentric dark irregular blotch with whitish regression-like areas, and a lighter tan, structureless extension, all on sun-damaged skin.

Small (~5 mm) brown macule with fairly regular reticular pattern, central darker hyperpigmentation with a few dots and mild asymmetry, fading periphery, on sun-damaged skin, most consistent with a nevus, though the eccentric dark center warrants some caution.

Two adjacent light-to-medium brown lesions with a fairly uniform reticular-globular pattern and no blue-white veil, atypical vessels or peripheral dots, which favors dysplastic nevi; the left lesion's asymmetry, irregular border and eccentric pink hypopigmented zone keep melanoma a real possibility.

Asymmetric, ill-defined pigmented patch on sun-damaged facial-type skin with irregular dark blotches, angulated/rhomboidal structures, and asymmetric follicular pigmentation, suggesting lentigo maligna melanoma.
Large asymmetric multicomponent lesion with irregular dark brown-black blotches, blue-white veil, atypical pigment network, regression-like white areas, and multiple colors on sun-damaged skin.
Small lesion with reddish-brown and dark brown-blue pigmentation, some irregular dots/globules and mild asymmetry, but compact size and fairly organized structure favor a dysplastic/benign nevus.

Small light-brown lesion with a slightly off-center darker reddish-brown area, faint ill-defined borders and mild asymmetry, but no atypical network, blue-white veil, regression or irregular dots, so a benign nevus is favored despite the purple marking and biopsy.

An asymmetric, lobulated lesion with an irregular border, a separate peripheral lobe, an atypical pigment network, and an eccentric darker grayish-blue central area suggesting regression or a multicomponent pattern.

Fairly symmetric orange-brown lesion with a regular peripheral border, uniform reticular/globular pattern and dotted pigment, and some central white structureless areas but no atypical network, blue-white veil or irregular streaks, favoring a benign (possibly dysplastic) nevus.

Irregular, asymmetric light-to-dark brown macule on sun-damaged facial skin with ill-defined borders, uneven pigment, annular-granular areas around follicles, and red vascular structures within it, suggesting lentigo maligna.

Small lesion with mildly irregular, angulated outline but uniform light-to-medium brown pigmentation, no blue-white veil, regression structures, or atypical network, most consistent with a benign nevus or lentigo.

Facial sun-damaged skin with a faint yellowish-tan, structureless pseudo-network around follicles, pink erythema and fine linear vessels; there are no grey rhomboids, dark asymmetric follicular pigmentation or annular-granular pattern, which favors a keratinocytic lesion over lentigo maligna, though that cannot be excluded.

Small (~4 mm) brown lesion with fairly uniform light-to-mid brown pigmentation, a faint reticular pattern, mild asymmetry and some irregular edges, but no blue-white veil, atypical vessels or regression structures, favoring a benign (dysplastic) nevus; overlying scale partly obscures the center.

Small (~4-5 mm) lesion on acral or volar-like skin showing a regular brown reticular/lattice-like pattern aligned with skin furrows, uniform color, no blue-white veil, atypical dots or regression, consistent with a benign acral nevus.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (dark brown, black, blue-gray, pink), blue-white veil and regression structures, irregular peripheral dots/globules, and a pink area with polymorphous vessels.

Small, ill-defined pink macule with clustered dotted/reddish vessels and faint peripheral brown pigment, set on freckled sun-damaged skin, with no atypical network, streaks, or blue-white structures; still, a featureless pink vascular lesion leaves amelanotic melanoma as a real possibility.

A large, poorly circumscribed lesion with an atypical, irregularly thickened pigment network, an eccentric irregular dark-brown blotch, multiple shades of brown, whitish regression-like areas and scattered fine vessels, suggestive of melanoma (possibly in situ) on sun-damaged skin.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (brown, blue-gray, pink/red), irregular eccentric dark blotches, blue-white veil areas, pink regression/milky-red zones with polymorphous vessels and irregular borders.

Pink-red largely amelanotic lesion with scale and keratin crust, milky-red areas, white structureless zones and irregular vessels, plus a dark pigmented area at the upper left; the picture is suspicious for amelanotic melanoma, though a keratinocytic tumor is also possible.

Small lesion (~3-4 mm) with an orange-brown crusted/keratotic component and an eccentric dark blue-brown blotch on hypopigmented skin, surrounded by multiple similar excoriated perifollicular papules, favoring a traumatized/inflamed benign lesion (e.g., irritated nevus or seborrheic keratosis) over melanoma, though the dark asymmetric blotch adds some concern.
Asymmetric lesion with an eccentric dark brown-purple area containing blue-gray dots/peppering, whitish regression-like zones, multiple colors and irregular dots and globules over a brown background.
An asymmetric nodular lesion shows white scar-like structureless areas, polymorphous linear vessels and blue-gray zones, with irregular satellite brown clods scattered in the surrounding skin.

A large, asymmetric light-brown lesion with an irregular, fragmented pigment network and irregular eccentric blotches, plus scar-like white regression areas and a pink zone of dotted and linear vessels, suggesting melanoma in situ on sun-damaged skin.
Asymmetric dark lesion with blue-white veil, irregular dark blotches and clods, and satellite-like irregular brown globules and patches at the periphery with multiple colors.

Large, asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (light-to-dark brown, gray-blue focal dots), irregular atypical network, extensive white regression-like structureless areas, and peppering suggest melanoma.

A pink, non-pigmented lesion with whitish scaly areas and a few fine linear vessels, but no pigment network, globules, streaks or atypical pigmentation, which fits a benign keratinocytic or inflammatory process; because amelanotic melanoma cannot be fully excluded from the image alone, the probability is not set lower.

Small, fairly symmetric light-to-medium brown lesion with a regular fine reticular network, darker central area, smooth fading borders, and no blue-white veil, regression, or atypical vessels, consistent with a benign nevus.
Asymmetric lesion with irregular, eccentric dark-brown blotches and peripheral dots/globules, a central pink-white regression-like area, and multiple colors, all concerning for melanoma.

Large, asymmetric lesion with irregular lobulated borders, multiple colors (dark brown-black, light brown, blue-gray, pink-white), a central blue-white veil with regression structures, eccentric dark blotches, and irregular dots — all strongly suggestive of melanoma.

Small, fairly symmetric light-to-medium brown lesion with a uniform reticular/globular pattern, a darker center fading to a regular periphery, a single color, and no blue-white veil, regression or atypical vessels, consistent with a benign nevus.

Small, fairly symmetric pinkish-tan macule with a faint delicate peripheral pigment network, central erythema and dotted vessels, no blue-white veil, atypical network or regression structures, on sun-damaged hairy skin, most consistent with a benign nevus.

Asymmetric lesion with irregular borders, multiple colors including a blue-gray area and focal darker eccentric blotch, regression-like whitish center, and atypical network with peripheral irregularity.

On sun-damaged skin, the lesion shows asymmetric, multifocal brown pigmentation with an eccentric dark blotch, angulated granular structures, and pinkish regression-like areas with fine vessels, suggesting lentigo maligna or melanoma.
Large asymmetric lesion with multiple browns, focal blue-gray granules/dots, irregular peripheral pigmentation and central whitish regression-like areas suggest melanoma.

Small, roughly symmetric, uniformly light-brown lesion with homogeneous center and regular peripheral dots/globules at the rim, no blue-white veil, regression, or atypical network, most consistent with a benign (likely growing) nevus.

Chronically sun-damaged skin with an ill-defined central darker brown-gray area showing irregular blotches, gray dots/granularity, and asymmetric pigmentation amid surrounding solar lentigines, suggestive of lentigo maligna.
